Need parse evidence. Source CLOUD-2018: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot." So one EU has two ranges; seeding randomly assigned to one range and not other. That suggests complementary assignment: one joint allocation selects seeded range, other receives complementary unseeded assignment. Both ranges not independently randomized; one gets seeded, other unseeded. So q1 = complementary_assignment. Check options: complementary_assignment "One joint allocation selects the seeded range, and the other range receives the complementary unseeded assignment." Yes.

q2: Does assigned-unseeded label by itself establish zero physical exposure to seeding material? Evidence: CLOUD-2014 slide 24 reports silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding. This indicates cross-range contamination: unseeded range may be physically exposed to seeding material from other range. Scope says "auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment." So assignment to unseeded range does not establish zero exposure; it's assignment only. Option "assignment_only": "No; it establishes the planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed." That matches. q2 = assignment_only.
